title: Pew Survey Across 36 Nations Reveals How the World Views India — and Its Rivalry With Pakistan
excerpt: A Pew Research Center survey of 42,151 people in 36 countries finds India viewed favorably in most nations, while Indians and Pakistanis continue to see each other as their greatest threat.
body:
• A median of 46% across surveyed countries hold a favorable view of India, compared with 34% unfavorable, with the strongest support in Israel (71%), Kenya (64%), and Nigeria (60%)
  • Indians are roughly three times more likely than Pakistanis to view the United States favorably, reflecting sharply divergent geopolitical orientations
  • 70% of Indians believe their country's global influence is rising, far above the 28% median in other countries surveyed
  • Indians and Pakistanis continue to identify each other as the greatest threat, with 73% of Indians holding an unfavorable view of Pakistan

A sweeping new Pew Research Center survey spanning 36 countries and more than 42,000 respondents has mapped global perceptions of India, revealing a country viewed favorably across most nations but locked in mutual hostility with Pakistan that colors both populations' worldview.

The findings, published as part of Pew's 2026 Global Attitudes Survey conducted from February 8 to May 13, come as India navigates the aftermath of Operation Sindoor and its broader assertiveness on the global stage.

India's Global Image: Mostly Positive, With Regional Variations

Across the nations surveyed, a median of 46% hold a favorable view of India, compared with 34% who view the country unfavorably. Israel leads with 71% favorable — reflecting the deepening I2U2 partnership and India's status as the top destination for Israeli arms exports. Kenya (64%) and Nigeria (60%) follow, with the United Kingdom at roughly six in ten.

South Africa stands out as a notable exception, where 51% hold an unfavorable view. In the Asia-Pacific, views are mixed: Japan and Australia lean unfavorable, while Indonesia holds a more positive view.

Among Indians themselves, confidence in the country's trajectory runs far higher than outside perceptions suggest. Some 70% of Indians believe their country's global influence has been growing — compared with a median of just 28% across 19 other countries who share that assessment, according to a companion Pew analysis.

India and Pakistan: Rivals With Divergent Worldviews

The survey underscores the depth of mutual hostility between the two nuclear-armed neighbors. About 73% of Indians hold an unfavorable view of Pakistan, including 57% who express a very unfavorable opinion. Only 19% of Indians view Pakistan positively.

The sentiment is reciprocated: 70% of Pakistanis hold a negative view of India, according to Pew's cross-national data. Both populations consistently identify each other as the greatest threat to their country.

"Indians are the least likely to have a positive opinion of Pakistan among the countries where this question was asked."

— Pew Research Center, 2026 Global Attitudes Survey

The geopolitical divergence extends well beyond bilateral animosity. Indians are roughly three times more likely than Pakistanis to view the United States favorably. Meanwhile, 57% of Indians view Russia positively — far above the 14% median across 22 other countries — and a majority of Indians hold an unfavorable view of China, making India the only middle-income country surveyed where that is the case.

Modi's Standing at Home and Abroad

PM Narendra Modi retains strong domestic support, with 79% of Indians holding a favorable view of him, including 55% who are very favorable. However, international perceptions are considerably more muted: only about 37% of respondents across 12 countries where the question was asked express confidence in Modi's foreign policy decisions.

Those who support the governing National Democratic Alliance parties are significantly more likely to believe India's influence is rising (77%) compared with non-supporters (60%). Men are also more likely than women to see India's power growing (71% vs. 65%).

Views of the US Divide India and Pakistan Further

The survey's broader findings on global attitudes toward the United States provide context for India's positioning. Across all 36 countries, a median of only 23% express confidence in President Trump's leadership. India, at 18% approval of Trump's tariff policies, reflects discomfort with trade actions that directly affect its economy — even as Indians remain among the most pro-American populations globally.

The share of people viewing the U.S. as a reliable partner has dropped steeply in many nations since 2022. In Canada, it fell from 83% to 35%. However, several middle-income nations including India, Kenya, and Sri Lanka continue to view the U.S. more favorably than the global median.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the estimated 4.4 million Indian Americans and millions more across the U.K., Canada, and the Gulf states, the findings carry practical implications. Favorable views of India in host countries correlate with warmer attitudes toward diaspora communities, while the sharp Pakistan-India hostility documented in the survey mirrors tensions that occasionally surface in diaspora settings abroad.

The survey was conducted during a period that overlapped with the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which began February 28 — an event Pew notes may have influenced some responses, particularly in Muslim-majority nations.
